cohort: 1,051 women seen in a tertiary urogynecology clinic between May 2016 and November 2018 with symptoms of pelvic floor dysfunction
finding: Vaginal laxity was more common in women who had given birth vaginally compared to those who had only had cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Vaginal laxity was found to be more prevalent in vaginally parous women, largely attributable to the first delivery, and instrumental delivery was not associated with increased VL compared to normal vaginal delivery.
